structured_output.pr_summary: Nine of the eleven shell-family defects share one shape. A shell line that makes a decision silently took the wrong branch, and nobody saw it because the check only ran the happy path or only ran on macOS. Examples: BSD-only stat/date/find -regex (#1900, #2092), pipefail plus grep -q SIGPIPE on Linux (#2174), awk filters that excluded nothing (#2039, #2208), the lsof header that always tripped a port guard (#1950), a `|| echo` probe that let DROP TABLE fire (#2220), a timeout wrapping a shell function (#1899), and a cd wrapper that broke relative paths (#2087). The registry already holds four narrow trigger rows and four narrow rule docs, one per tool. Each new tool adds a new row after it bites. This adds one umbrella forced-trigger row: any decision-making shell line must have a one-shot check, run on the Ubuntu runner, that drives both the pass and the fail branch. The narrow rows stay as worked examples. #1897 and #1963 are PHP/import-path defects that ended up in this family by mistake, and this row does not cover them.
